inputs.text: Father Bernard Domini, superior of the Missionary Family of Notre-Dame, has been convicted under France’s new law on “psychological subjection.” Protecting people from coercion matters, but a law with such a broad-sounding target also raises serious civil-liberties concerns: the state must not be allowed to punish belief or association without clear, rigorous safeguards. The alarm from religious communities and civil-liberties advocates should be taken seriously. A just response to harm must protect vulnerable people without handing institutions vague powers over private life.
